key_insight: Compact multimodal language models performed best for pulmonary embolism risk assessment when CT pulmonary angiography was combined with EHR evidence, especially for Gemma4 E4B and E2B.
clinical_relevance: This suggests efficient AI tools could help support earlier PE diagnosis and risk stratification by integrating imaging and longitudinal clinical context.
method: Built INSPECT-based benchmark with 23,248 CTPA studies from 19,402 patients
Reformulated 8 diagnostic and prognostic PE tasks as structured clinical QA
Compared efficient MLLMs under CTPA-only, EHR-only, and CTPA+EHR settings with zero-shot and few-shot prompting
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that models improved most with EHR availability, and that diagnosis tasks outperformed prognostic tasks, particularly readmission prediction.
watch_item: Performance was lower on prognostic tasks than diagnosis, so real-world use would need careful validation before relying on these models for outcome prediction.
paper_title: Efficient Multimodal Clinical Question Answering for Pulmonary Embolism Risk Assessment
